# 2 Samuel Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 189v–190v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_018_page_001.jpg, 2SA_018_page_002.jpg, 2SA_018_page_003.jpg

---

**1** David organized the troops who were with him, appointing commanders over units of a thousand and units of a hundred. **2** He divided the army into three columns: one third under Joab, one third under Abishai son of Zeruiah (Joab's brother), and one third under Ittai the Gittite. The king told his men, "I will march out with you myself."

**3** But the men said, "No! You must not come out with us. If we have to retreat, they won't care about us. Even if half of us die, they won't care. But you are worth ten thousand of us. It's better for you to stay in the city and send us support from there."

**4** The king said, "I will do whatever you think best." So he stood beside the gate as the entire army marched out in their companies and regiments.

**5** The king gave orders to Joab, Abishai, and Ittai: "For my sake, be gentle with young Absalom." The whole army heard the king give this command about Absalom to every officer.

**6** The army advanced into the field to engage the Israelites, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim. **7** The Israelite forces were crushed that day by David's men. The casualties were enormous — twenty thousand dead. **8** The fighting spread across the whole countryside, and the forest claimed more lives that day than the sword did.

**9** Absalom suddenly came face to face with David's men. He was riding his mule, and the mule passed under the thick branches of a great oak tree. Absalom's head got caught fast in the oak, and he was left dangling between heaven and earth while the mule kept going beneath him.

**10** One of the soldiers saw this and reported to Joab: "I just saw Absalom hanging from an oak tree!"

**11** Joab snapped at the man, "You saw him? Why didn't you strike him down right there? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a warrior's belt!"

**12** The man replied, "Even if you put a thousand pieces of silver in my hand, I would never raise a hand against the king's son. We all heard the king command you and Abishai and Ittai: 'Protect young Absalom for my sake.'

**13** If I had killed him — and nothing stays hidden from the king — you would have left me to face the consequences alone."

**14** Joab said, "I'm not going to waste time with you." He grabbed three wooden staves and drove them into Absalom's chest while Absalom was still alive, pinned in the oak.

**15** Then ten of Joab's armor-bearers closed in around Absalom, struck him, and finished him off.

**16** Joab sounded the ram's horn, and the troops pulled back from chasing the Israelites, because Joab called off the pursuit.

**17** They took Absalom's body and threw it into a deep pit in the forest, and piled a huge mound of stones over it. Meanwhile, all the Israelites scattered to their homes.

**18** During his lifetime, Absalom had set up a stone pillar for himself in the King's Valley, since he said, "I have no son to carry on my name." He named the pillar after himself, and to this day it is known as Absalom's Monument.

**19** Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run and bring the king the news that the LORD has delivered him from his enemies!"

**20** But Joab told him, "You are not the man to carry news today. Some other day, perhaps — but not today, because the king's son is dead."

**21** Joab told the Cushite messenger, "Go — tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed to Joab and took off running.

**22** But Ahimaaz pressed Joab again: "Whatever happens, please let me run too — after the Cushite!" Joab said, "Why do you want to run, my son? You won't get any reward for the news you'd carry."

**23** "I don't care — let me run!" So Joab said, "Run." Ahimaaz took the route through the Jordan plain and outran the Cushite.

**24** David was sitting between the inner and outer gates of the city. The watchman had climbed to the roof of the gate on the wall. He looked out and saw a man running alone. **25** The watchman called down and told the king. David said, "If he's alone, he has news." The runner kept getting closer.

**26** Then the watchman spotted a second runner. He called down to the gatekeeper, "There's another man running alone!" The king said, "He must have news too."

**27** The watchman said, "The first one runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok." The king said, "He's a good man — he must be bringing good news."

**28** Ahimaaz called out as he approached, "All is well!" He bowed low before the king, face to the ground, and said, "Praise the LORD your God, who has handed over the men who raised their hands against my lord the king!"

**29** The king asked, "Is young Absalom safe?" Ahimaaz answered, "When Joab sent me off, I saw some kind of commotion, but I don't know what it was about."

**30** The king said, "Step aside and wait here." He stepped aside and stood there.

**31** Then the Cushite arrived. "Good news for my lord the king!" the Cushite said. "The LORD has vindicated you today against all who rose up against you!"

**32** The king asked the Cushite, "Is young Absalom safe?" The Cushite replied, "May all the enemies of my lord the king — and all who rise against you to do you harm — end up like that young man."

**33** The king was shattered. He went up to the room above the gate and wept. And as he walked, he kept saying, "O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you — O Absalom, my son, my son!"

---
*— PNEUMA*
